summary: an activate or deactivate has no matching counterpart
help: Pair every activate with a deactivate for the same participant, or use the + and - message shorthands.
rationale: An activation left open draws a dangling activation bar that runs to the end of the diagram.

summary: a participant is used in a message before it is declared
help: Declare the participant above its first message.
rationale: Mermaid auto-creates undeclared participants, so the drawn order follows message order instead of the intended declaration order.

summary: the same participant or actor id is declared twice
help: Declare each participant once.
rationale: A repeated declaration makes the lifeline order and labels ambiguous.

summary: A message line lacks a : before the message text
help: Use: A->>B: Message text
rationale: Without the colon the text after the actor is not a message, so nothing is drawn.

summary: A note statement is incomplete or missing the colon
rationale: Without the colon the note text has no place to start.

summary: Unknown or malformed arrow token in a message.
rationale: Only the listed arrow tokens exist in the grammar, so an unknown one breaks the message.

summary: An else appears outside an alt block
help: Use: alt Condition … else … end
rationale: else only means something inside alt, so a stray else misparses the frame structure.

summary: An and appears outside a par block
help: Example: par … and … end (parallel branches).
rationale: and only splits branches inside par, so a stray and misparses the frame structure.

summary: An end appears with no open block
help: Remove this end or start a block above.
rationale: A stray end closes nothing, so the parser loses track of the frame structure.

summary: A block such as alt, opt, loop, par, rect, critical, break, or box is not closed with end
help: Add 'end' on a new line after the block contents.
rationale: The block stays open to the end of the file, so everything after it is swallowed into the frame.

summary: An else appears inside a critical block; use option
help: Replace with: option <label> Example: option Retry
rationale: critical sections branch with option, not else, so an else misparses the section.

summary: The autonumber statement has an invalid form
help: Use: autonumber | autonumber off | autonumber 10 10
rationale: A malformed autonumber statement is dropped, so numbering silently stops.

summary: A non-numeric value is used for the autonumber start or step
help: Use numbers: autonumber 10 or autonumber 10 10 (start and step).
rationale: The grammar reads numbers here, and a word cannot be coerced into one.

summary: Extra tokens appear after autonumber on the same line
help: Example: autonumber 10 10\nparticipant A
rationale: Only the start and step belong on the line, so a declaration after autonumber is dropped.

summary: The create statement is missing the target or has invalid syntax
help: Example: create participant B
rationale: A create without a valid target cannot introduce the actor.

summary: The destroy statement is missing the target or has invalid syntax
help: Examples: destroy participant A  |  destroy actor B
rationale: A destroy without a valid target cannot end the actor's lifeline.

summary: The create statement ends without a participant or actor name
help: Use: create participant A  or  create actor B
rationale: There is nothing to create, so the statement is dropped.

summary: The destroy statement ends without a participant or actor name
help: Use: destroy participant A  or  destroy actor B
rationale: There is nothing to destroy, so the statement is dropped.

summary: Participant or actor names, aliases, or block labels contain backslash-escaped quotes, which Mermaid does not support
help: Example: participant "Logger "debug"" as L
rationale: Mermaid has no backslash escape inside names, so the backslash reaches the output.

summary: A double-quoted participant or actor name or label contains another double quote
help: Example: participant "Logger "debug"" as L
rationale: The inner quote ends the name early and corrupts the rest of the line.

summary: A participant or actor name or alias starts a quote but does not close it
help: Close the quote: participant "Bob" or participant Alice as "Alias"
rationale: The rest of the line is read as the name until the parser gives up.

summary: The file does not start with sequenceDiagram
help: Start with: sequenceDiagram
rationale: Detection resolves the kind from the header, so this condition is already reported as common/unknown-diagram-kind.
reason: the kind comes from the header in the kinds table, so a missing or unknown header is common/unknown-diagram-kind

summary: A title, accTitle, or accDescr line appears in a sequence diagram
help: Remove this line to match mermaid-cli.
rationale: The CLI rejects these lines for sequence diagrams, so keeping them breaks parity.

summary: A properties: line appears in a sequence diagram
help: Remove the properties: line to match mermaid-cli.
rationale: The CLI rejects this line for sequence diagrams, so keeping it breaks parity.

summary: A details: line appears in a sequence diagram
help: Remove the details: line to match mermaid-cli.
rationale: The CLI rejects this line for sequence diagrams, so keeping it breaks parity.

summary: An activate is not balanced by a matching deactivate for the same actor
help: Add deactivate A after the active section.
rationale: The activation bar stays open to the end of the diagram.

summary: A create line is not immediately followed by a message involving the created actor
help: Add a creating message to or from 'X' immediately after the create line.
rationale: The actor is created but never used, so the create has no visible effect.

summary: A message line activates a target that is already active
help: Remove '+' or deactivate first: deactivate Target
rationale: A second activation of an active actor is an authoring mistake and corrupts the activation stack.

summary: A message line deactivates a target that has no active activation
help: Remove '-' or ensure 'activate Target' occurred before.
rationale: Deactivating an inactive actor is an authoring mistake and corrupts the activation stack.

summary: The file contains and but no par
help: Start a parallel section with: par … and … end
rationale: An and with no par has nothing to split, so it is probably a misplaced or mistyped block.

summary: The file contains else but no alt
help: Use: alt Condition … else … end
rationale: An else with no alt has nothing to split, so it is probably a misplaced or mistyped block.

summary: A free-form line starts with - outside a supported statement
help:
Wrap free-form text in a note block, for example:
    Note over A : Item 1
    Note over A
      - Item 1
      - Item 2
    end note
rationale: Bullets are only read inside note blocks, so a bare bullet line is dropped.
